sources.entry: JavaScript: _Build Your Own Module Bundler - Minipack_

summary.one_liner: Minipack is a short, educational JavaScript implementation of a simplified module bundler, meant to show how tools like Webpack, Browserify, and Parcel work internally.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes Minipack as a simplified but reasonably accurate example of a modern module bundler, written in JavaScript. Its stated purpose is to explain how most bundlers work under the hood. The entry point is src/minipack.js, which the README says contains code comments explaining what each part is trying to achieve. Running the script with node is the way to see it in action. The README does not list specific bundling features beyond this, so the exact capabilities are best confirmed in the source.
use_cases: learning how module bundlers work internally
understanding what Webpack or Parcel do under the hood
studying dependency graph and bundle generation
notable: Deliberately small, commented implementation intended as a learning resource
Entry point is a single file, src/minipack.js
Mirrors concepts from Webpack, Browserify, and Parcel without being a production tool
README links to AST Explorer, Babel REPL, Babylon, and the Babel Plugin Handbook for background reading
caveats: Explicitly a simplified example, not a production-ready bundler
README gives little detail on supported features or input options
